entries.title: Manifest lacks enforceable file operation model
entries.description: The spec requires deterministic planning, checksum verification for all changed files, generated-file ownership, and rollback snapshots, but the manifest schema only shows packages, migrations, a generic checksums object, and an optional signature. There is no canonical file list, artifact location, target path rule, prior checksum expectation, executable bit metadata, or ownership marker from which the updater can safely derive concrete operations. Under adversarial reading, different implementations could invent incompatible operation derivation rules while still claiming to satisfy the spec.

entries.title: Customer no-policy default is contradictory
entries.description: The spec says customer installs default to `stable` with `safe_additive` for templates, registries, and docs, but the Open Decisions section asks whether customer installs should default to `stable` or `pinned` when no explicit customer policy exists. It also says customer policy ambiguity is mitigated by requiring `UPDATE_POLICY.md` plus machine-readable local policy before apply. These statements leave the most safety-sensitive case, missing or incomplete customer policy, unresolved.

entries.title: Approval gate artifact is underspecified
entries.description: The spec repeatedly requires approval for risky, executable, permission-affecting, destructive, and customer-visible changes, but leaves the approval artifact format as an open decision. P2 and P3 behavior depends on knowing whether approval is a CLI token, signed file, or control-plane record, and what exactly it authorizes. Without this, an implementation might accidentally treat approval as broad permission to recompute or mutate a plan rather than permission to apply a specific precomputed plan.

entries.title: Path safety rules are implicit
entries.description: The spec forbids telemetry paths and emphasizes preserving local work, but it does not explicitly constrain update target paths. A malicious or malformed manifest could reference absolute paths, parent-directory traversal, symlinks, or files outside the OS root unless the path validation invariant is stated. Checksum verification alone does not prevent writing to the wrong location.

entries.title: UPDATE_POLICY.md consistency is not machine-enforceable
entries.description: The spec requires agentic-os.local.json and UPDATE_POLICY.md to agree on channel, policy mode, environment, and auto-update before customer safe_additive apply. However UPDATE_POLICY.md is described as human-readable, with no required frontmatter, canonical fields, schema, or parsing rule. Under adversarial reading, one implementation could treat prose as sufficient while another fails closed, and customer auto-update safety would depend on parser interpretation rather than a crisp invariant.

entries.title: Manifest digest canonicalization is underspecified
entries.description: The manifest includes `manifest_digest` inside the JSON whose digest it claims to represent, and also has an optional `signature` field. The spec does not define whether the digest covers the full manifest, excludes `manifest_digest`, excludes `signature`, or uses a canonical JSON serialization. Under adversarial reading, manifest verification can become impossible or implementation-specific while still satisfying the prose.

entries.title: Registry merge content digest conflicts with local additions
entries.description: `merge_registry_additive` requires a `content_digest` described as the post-merge content digest, but additive registry merging is supposed to preserve existing local entries. If a customer registry already contains allowed local additions, the final post-merge file digest cannot be known by the canonical manifest unless the manifest also knows every local registry state. This creates pressure either to reject safe local additions or to overwrite them, both contrary to the safety model.
